description: Implementation of the 'Janaridhma' (SL-PULSE) Project to strengthen Citizen-Centred Governance and Frontline Public Service Delivery through the Regional Administrative System
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-24 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka’s Regional Administrative Structure consists of 25 District Secretariats and 341 Divisional Secretariats. This institutional system provides a range of essential public services including community development, social security, State land administration, disaster management, civil registration, pension related services and other citizen-centered administrative functions. At present, there is no national mechanism in place to systematically collect and evaluate citizens' feedback and experiences on accessibility to services and the quality and efficiency of those services. Therefore, considering the need to establish a mechanism for this purpose, the 'Janaridhma' (SL-PULSE) project has been planned to be implemented under the financial and technical assistance provided by the United Nations Development Programme to conduct Sri Lanka’s first citizen feedback survey on Public Services. The relevant survey is to be conducted island-wide, involving between 13,000 - 15,000 citizens, covering seven (07) key areas of citizen participation, citizen accountability, corruption reduction, public administration procedures, public services, environment and digitalization, under the levels of open public participation, community-based survey and random survey. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government to implement the 'Janaridhma' (SL-PULSE) project enabling to analyze the data obtained and implement the necessary reforms to increase the efficiency and transparency of the provision of relevant public services, was approved by the Cabinet.
